## Description of variables 

Quantitative Easing Shocks (Source: APP_breakdown_history.csv from the ECB website): 
The monthly net amount in euro millions of ECB asset purchases

Corporate borrowing rates (Source: ECB data portal): Weighted average annual interest rates of new loans for corporations in each country 

## Set-up & Loading data 

```{r}

here::i_am("data_management_project.Rproj")
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

```

Load Data: Historical data of asset puchases by the ECB (Downloaded from the webpage https://www.ecb.europa.eu/mopo/implement/app/html/index.en.html) & Data cleaning

Data cleaning: Remove useless data & Adding dates & Converting variables to proper formats

```{r}

#We load the .csv file directly downloaded from the ECB website titled "APP_breakdown_history.csv"
QE_mnet <- read_csv(here("data", "APP_breakdown_history.csv"))

#The title row and first two rows of the original .csv file are empty except for some textual descriptions of the file, therefore: 

#First, we remove the first two rows 
QE_mnet <- QE_mnet |>
  slice(-(1:2))|>
  slice(-(135:137))
#Second, the names of the variables need to be manually added. 

names(QE_mnet)[1] <- paste("Year")
names(QE_mnet)[2] <- paste("Month")
names(QE_mnet)[3] <- paste("ABSPP") #Asset-backed securities purchase programme
names(QE_mnet)[4] <- paste("CBPP3") #Covered bond purchase programme 3
names(QE_mnet)[5] <- paste("CSPP") #Corporate Sector purchase programme
names(QE_mnet)[6] <- paste("PSPP") #Public Sector purchase programme

#All data starting from the 7th column describe quarterly adjustments and total holdings, which, for this project specifically, are useless, which is why we remove them. 
QE_mnet <- QE_mnet|>
  dplyr::select(1:6)

#In the original .csv, the year column is empty for all months except for the first month of each year, and there is no date column. Therefore, dates need to be manually added to facilitate later computation. 


#First, we add the missing years. 

QE_mnet <- QE_mnet |>
  fill(Year, .direction = "down")

#Second, we manually create a date column titled "DATE" (because later we will merge with other datasets with a date column of the same title) containing the last day of each month, for all values are calculated on the last day of the month

QE_mnet <- QE_mnet |>
  mutate(
    Month_num = match(Month, month.name),
    Month_num = ifelse(is.na(Month_num), match(Month, month.abb), Month_num),
    date_first = make_date(year = Year, month = Month_num, day = 1),
    last_day = days_in_month(date_first),
    DATE = paste0(Year,"/", Month_num, "/", last_day)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(-Month_num, -date_first, -last_day)


QE_mnet <- QE_mnet|>
  mutate(DATE = as.Date(DATE, format = "%Y/%m/%d"))


#Last, since we are only interested in the magnitude of quantitative easing carried out by the BCE, the specific amounts of each type of asset are irrelevant for this project. Therefore, we add them to get the ECB's monthly net purchase value. 

#First, we convert them from character to numerical format 
QE_mnet <- QE_mnet|>
  mutate(ABSPP = as.numeric(ABSPP),
         CBPP3 = as.numeric(CBPP3),
         CSPP = as.numeric(CSPP),
         PSPP = as.numeric(PSPP))
#Second, we add them together
QE_mnet <- QE_mnet|>
  mutate(Mnet = ABSPP+CBPP3+CSPP+PSPP)


```

Loading Data: Corporate borrowing rates per country (downloaded from the ECB data portal) 

Data cleaning: Renaming variables & Pivoting
```{r}

corp_int <- read_csv(here("data","corp_int.csv"))

library(stringr)

#The original .csv file is in wide format, with one column for each country. The problem is that the name of each column is a string containing the letter code of the variable and the iso2 code of the country. Therefore, we extract the iso2 codes from the string. 

corp_int <- corp_int |>
  rename_with(~ ifelse(
    str_detect(., "MIR\\.M\\.[A-Z]{2}\\."),
    str_extract(., "(?<=MIR\\.M\\.)[A-Z]{2}(?=\\.)"),
    .
  ))


#The previous function does not the code "U2" (which represents the EU) because it does not contain only letters from the alphabet, therefore, we manually add it. 
names(corp_int)[23] <- paste("U2")

#We change the date format and remove the useless "TIME PERIOD" column 
corp_int <- corp_int|>
  mutate(DATE = as.Date(DATE, format = "%Y/%m/%d"))

corp_int <- corp_int|>dplyr::select(!`TIME PERIOD`)


#We pivot from long to wide, so that now we have observations in country-months
corp_int <- corp_int|>
    pivot_longer(
    cols = -DATE,
    names_to = "Country",
    values_to = "int"
  )

```

Merging corporate interest rates & QE datasets 

```{r}

qe_int <- QE_mnet|>
  left_join(
    corp_int
  )

```

Graphical representation of target variable

```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

#Preliminary visusalization of varying differences between corporate borrowing rates of each country and the EMU average 

emu_avg_rates <- corp_int |>
  drop_na() |>
  filter(Country == "U2") |>
  dplyr::select(DATE, EMU_Avg = int)

corp_int_deviation <- corp_int |>
  drop_na() |>
  filter(Country != "U2") |>
  left_join(emu_avg_rates, by = "DATE") |>
  mutate(Deviation = int - EMU_Avg) |>
  dplyr::select(-EMU_Avg)

corp_int_deviation|>
  ggplot(aes(x = DATE, y = Deviation, group = Country, color = Country)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Corporate Borrowing Rate Deviation from EMU Average",
    x = "Month/Year",
    y = "Deviation from EMU Average Rate (Percentage Points)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

#Preliminary visualization of the cross-country differences between their relationships with QE amounts

library(ggeffects)

qe_int <- qe_int |>
  arrange(Country, DATE)

qe_int <- qe_int |>
  group_by(Country) |>
  mutate(Mnet_lag1 = lag(Mnet, 1)) |> 
  ungroup()

qe_nona <- drop_na(qe_int)

fit = lm(formula = int ~Mnet_lag1*Country, data=qe_nona)
pred = ggpredict(fit, terms = c("Mnet_lag1","Country"))
plot(pred) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "turbo") +
  ggtitle(NULL)

```


## Regression

```{r}

library(AER)       # For ivreg (2SLS)
library(plm)       # For Panel Data structures
library(tidyverse) # For data cleaning
library(stargazer) # For regression tables


core <- data|>filter(Group == "Core")
p_core <- pdata.frame(core, index = c("Country", "DATE"))

core_2sls <- ivreg(int ~ HICP + LT10Y + ST3M + Mnet | 
                    HICP + LT10Y + ST3M + lag(Mnet, 1), 
                    data = p_core)

summary(core_2sls, diagnostics = TRUE)

peri <- data|>filter(Group == "Periphery")
p_peri <- pdata.frame(peri, index = c("Country", "DATE"))

peri_2sls <- ivreg(int ~ HICP + LT10Y + ST3M + Mnet | 
                    HICP + LT10Y + ST3M + lag(Mnet, 1), 
                    data = p_peri)

summary(peri_2sls, diagnostics = TRUE)

other <- data|>filter(Group == "Periphery")
p_other <- pdata.frame(other, index = c("Country", "DATE"))

other_2sls <- ivreg(int ~ HICP + LT10Y + ST3M + Mnet | 
                    HICP + LT10Y + ST3M + lag(Mnet, 1), 
                    data = p_other)

summary(other_2sls, diagnostics = TRUE)

```

##Regressions by country

```{r}

library(broom)

countries <- unique(reg_data$Country)
country_results <- list()

print(paste("Starting loop for", length(countries), "countries..."))

for (ctry in countries) {
  
  # Filter for country
  temp_data <- reg_data |>dplyr::filter(Country == ctry)
  
  # Remove rows with any NAs in our specific variables
  clean_data <- temp_data|>
    tidyr::drop_na(int, HICP, LT10Y, ST3M, Mnet)
  
  num_obs <- nrow(clean_data)
  
  if(num_obs > 10) {
    # Try the regression
    try_result <- try({
      model <- lm(int ~ HICP + LT10Y + ST3M + Mnet, data = clean_data)
      country_results[[ctry]] <- broom::tidy(model) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(country = ctry)
    }, silent = FALSE)
    
    if(inherits(try_result, "try-error")) {
      print(paste("!", ctry, "failed during lm() calculation."))
    } else {
      print(paste("✓", ctry, "processed successfully with", num_obs, "rows."))
    }
    
  } else {
    print(paste("X", ctry, "skipped: only has", num_obs, "valid rows."))
  }
}

# Combine
if(length(country_results) > 0) {
  final_coefficients <- dplyr::bind_rows(country_results)
  print("Success! 'final_coefficients' is now populated.")
} else {
  print("ERROR: All countries failed or were skipped.")
}

final_coefficients|> filter(term == "Mnet", p.value < 0.05)

```

##ARMA or VAR testing

#First, ensure stationarity using first differences

```{r}

library(vars)
library(tseries)


model_data <- data

model_data <- model_data |>
  dplyr::select(DATE, Mnet, Country, int, HICP, ST3M, LT10Y)|>
  mutate(int = int*100,#Convert interest rates to basis points
         Mnet = Mnet/1000) #Convert quantitative easing amount from millions to billions

prep_country_var <- function(data, country_code) {
  country_df <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(Country == country_code) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(DATE) %>%
    dplyr::select(int, Mnet, HICP, ST3M) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>%
    # Calculate differences - this creates ONE row of NAs at the top
    dplyr::mutate(across(everything(), ~ .x - dplyr::lag(.x))) %>%
    # CRITICAL: Remove ALL rows containing any NA
    tidyr::drop_na() 
  
  # Final check: if the dataframe is empty after dropping NAs, return NULL
  if (nrow(country_df) < 5) return(NULL)
  
  return(as.ts(country_df))
}

```

Second, create a for loop to fit a VAR model for each country

```{r}

countries <- unique(model_data$Country)
var_results <- list()

for (ctry in countries) {
  # 1. Prepare time series
  ts_data <- prep_country_var(model_data, ctry)
  
  # 2. Select optimal lags (usually based on AIC)
  lag_select <- VARselect(ts_data, lag.max = 6, type = "both")
  opt_lag <- lag_select$selection["AIC(n)"]
  
  # 3. Run the VAR
  try({
    model_var <- VAR(ts_data, p = opt_lag, type = "both")
    var_results[[ctry]] <- model_var
    print(paste("✓ VAR completed for", ctry))
  }, silent = TRUE)
}

```

IRF for Italy 

```{r}

# 1. Check variance first (If any are 0, the VAR will fail)
apply(prep_country_var(model_data, "IT"), 2, var)

# 2. Re-run a "Restricted" VAR for Italy specifically to fix the math
# We force p = 2 to ensure the matrix is stable
ts_it <- prep_country_var(model_data, "IT")
model_it_stable <- VAR(ts_it, p = 2, type = "const")

# 3. Run the IRF with 'ortho = FALSE' 
# This bypasses the Cholesky decomposition error if the correlations are the issue
irf_it <- irf(model_it_stable, 
              impulse = "Mnet", 
              response = "int", 
              n.ahead = 10, 
              ortho = FALSE, # This is the key fix for the chol.default error
              boot = TRUE)

plot(irf_it, main = "Shock to QE: Impact on Italian Corporate Rates (Stable)")

```
